its location; copy your own practice-file path. Stop manually at the listed end. Public title, creator, runtime and

The job of this lesson
Find a file again after you close it. This sounds small, but every later data task depends on
knowing which input you opened and where you saved the result. You need a Windows
computer and a mouse or touchpad. You do not need Excel, SQL or programming yet. A phone is
useful for reading beside your computer; do the file practice on the computer.
Words before actions
Word
Plain meaning
Example
File
One named item containing
information
a shopping list saved as list.txt
Folder
A container that groups files
and other folders
a folder called practice
Drive
A storage location Windows
gives a label
the C: drive
Path
The directions to a file or folder
C:\Users\Ashish\Documents\DE_Study
Parent
The folder immediately outside
your current folder
DE_Study is the parent of practice
A file is like a particular notebook. A folder is like the shelf holding it. Two shelves can each
contain a notebook named list.txt. The name alone does not tell you which one you are holding.
A path includes the shelf information. In a Windows path, each backslash separates one level.
Your account name might be different from Ashish. Do not type somebody else's full path and
expect it to exist.
Follow with me once
Press Windows key + E to open File Explorer, the application for browsing files. Open Documents
from the left side. If it is not visible, open Home and find Documents there. A Documents folder
might be managed by OneDrive; that is why the actual path on your machine may differ from a
printed example.
Right-click an empty area, choose New, then Folder. Name the folder DE_Study. Double-click it
to go inside. Create three folders named raw, practice and evidence. Give each a different job:
raw keeps original inputs; practice holds work you can change; evidence holds attempts and
explanations you want to keep. Do not put your personal documents into the course raw folder.
Click the address bar above the file list. Copy the displayed full path with Ctrl+C and paste it
into a blank Notepad document. Then write: "raw keeps my original; practice holds my working
copy." Save the document as folder-map.txt inside evidence. In Save As, check the destination
as well as the filename. Close Notepad. Return to evidence and open folder-map.txt. You have
proved that the file exists at the location you intended, rather than only remaining open in an
application.
What you should see and understand
DE_Study contains three folders. The evidence folder contains folder-map.txt. Opening raw does
not show that file, because raw is a different folder. A folder can be empty without being broken.
Clicking the Back arrow returns to a previous location; clicking the parent breadcrumb moves
one level outward. Those are different actions when you have visited several locations.
Do not memorize C:\Users\Ashish. Learn to obtain your own actual path. Later a program will
need this same information to read data. A correct filename in the wrong folder still produces a
file-not-found problem.
If your screen differs
If the file seems missing, inspect the address bar before searching the entire computer. You
may be in Downloads rather than evidence. If you accidentally created DE_Study inside
DE_Study, move your empty practice folders to the intended parent using Cut and Paste; first
inspect both locations. If a folder is managed by your school or employer and you cannot create
files there, use a location where your account permits personal study files. Do not change
system permissions to complete this exercise.
Your independent practice
Inside practice, create a folder named first_attempt. In Notepad, create location.txt containing
the full path of first_attempt. Save it there, close it, and reopen it from File Explorer. In your
saved attempt file, write the path and explain why evidence\location.txt and
practice\first_attempt\location.txt would be different files.
Changed retry - after your first review
Create a folder called second_attempt beside first_attempt, not inside it. Save another
location.txt there containing "second attempt". Reopen each location.txt and explain which path
leads to which contents.
Ready-made revision
A filename identifies an item within a folder. A full path includes its location. Close and reopen to
check a save. Keep original inputs separate from working copies. You may move on when you
can find both retry files and explain their locations without guessing.
Evidence to keep: your attempt, the observed result and its explanation. Save the first attempt before
opening DE00-01 in the Explained Reviews book. After review, solve the changed retry and keep it as a
separate attempt.

Instructor demonstration: Windows 11 File Explorer for Beginners, 10:40-12:57. Inspect name, type and size
columns. This segment does not teach CSV, JSON or extension toggling; the book explains those separately.
Stop manually at the listed end. Public title, creator, runtime and published chapter boundaries inspected; full

The job of this lesson
Recognize what sort of file you are handling before you open or rename it. First complete
DE00-01. You will use Notepad and File Explorer. We will inspect a tiny table as text; you do not
need to understand all its business meaning yet.
Words before actions
Word
Plain meaning
Example
Extension
The ending after the last dot in
a filename
.txt in note.txt
Format
The rules used to arrange a
file's contents
CSV uses separators between fields
Plain text
Characters without a
workbook's formatting features
a note readable in Notepad
CSV
A text format commonly used
for rows and columns
orders.csv
XLSX
An Excel workbook format
practice.xlsx
A file extension is a label, not a machine that changes the contents. Renaming a photograph to
photo.xlsx does not turn it into a spreadsheet. Applications usually use the extension to decide
how to open a file, which is why an incorrect label can cause confusing errors.
Look at a real small file
In Windows 11 File Explorer, use View, Show, File name extensions. In other layouts, look for File
name extensions on the View tab. Check that you can now see .txt after folder-map. Extensions
are part of the filename; keep them when you rename the main name.
Open Notepad and type the following three lines. Commas separate values within each row.
Each new line starts another row.
item,quantity
Notebook,2
Pen,3
Save in practice as tiny-orders.csv. In Notepad's Save As dialog, select All files if needed so it
does not add .txt after .csv. Leave a normal text encoding such as UTF-8. UTF-8 is a common
way of representing characters as stored bytes; you do not need its internal rules now. Close
Notepad. In File Explorer, confirm the exact name is tiny-orders.csv, not tiny-orders.csv.txt.
Open it with Notepad using Open with. The commas should still be visible. Opening a CSV in a
spreadsheet may display those same values in separate cells. The file did not need to change
for two applications to show it differently.
Understand the limits
A CSV does not preserve multiple workbook sheets, colours or chart objects. It also does not
provide a workbook's reliable per-cell formatting instructions. An application may guess that
0007 means the number 7 when importing it. We will protect identifiers in M01. XLSX can store
sheets, formulas and formatting. JSON is another text data format: it labels values using names,
such as {"item":"Pen","quantity":3}. A ZIP contains packaged files; extract it before working. A
PDF presents pages for reading. An EXE can run a Windows program, so it is different from a
simple reading file.
If something looks wrong
If Windows warns that changing an extension may make a file unusable, cancel unless you
deliberately need to correct an incorrect extension and understand the contents. If your CSV
opens as text in one column, first inspect its separators and the import settings; do not delete
commas at random. If a downloaded file claims to be a document but its real final extension is
.exe, do not open it as a lesson document.
Your independent practice
Create stock.csv with a header item,count and two rows: Folder,1 and Marker,2. Reopen it in
Notepad. Record its full filename, its three lines and whether it can preserve a chart. Explain
why renaming stock.csv to stock.xlsx would not create a workbook.
Changed retry - after your first review
Create a plain text file named names.txt containing Asha and Ravi on separate lines. Make a
copy named names-backup.txt. Explain what changes if you rename only the copy to people.txt,
and what does not change.
Ready-made revision
Extension: a filename label. Format: the contents' structure. Renaming is not conversion. CSV is
useful for simple data exchange; XLSX keeps workbook features. Show extensions and inspect
the actual final ending before opening unfamiliar files.

Instructor demonstration: Windows 11 File Explorer for Beginners, 17:01-24:25. Watch the toolbar and
copying/moving files. ZIP extraction is taught step by step in the book; it is not covered by this assigned
segment. Stop manually at the listed end. Public title, creator, runtime and published chapter boundaries

The job of this lesson
Make a safe working copy of a course input and prove that you kept the original. Complete the
previous two lessons. Use the course package you downloaded; an additional tiny archive,
labs/M00/file-practice.zip, is included for this exercise.
Words before actions
Word
Plain meaning
Why it matters
Download
Save a remote file on your
device
a browser tab is not your local copy
Archive
A file that packages other files
a ZIP can contain several folders
Extract
Unpack an archive into ordinary
files
edit the extracted working files
Copy
Make another item while
keeping the first
suitable for preserving inputs
Move
Change an item's location
the item leaves its old location
Imagine receiving a sealed parcel containing a notebook. Opening the parcel lets you see the
notebook. Writing on a photocopy preserves the notebook. A ZIP is the parcel; extraction
unpacks it; copying makes the version you will edit. These are three different actions.
Follow with me once
After downloading this batch, find its ZIP in your browser's Downloads list or File Explorer's
Downloads folder. Wait until the download finishes. Right-click the ZIP and choose Extract All.
Select a destination you can find again, such as DE_Study\practice. Open the extracted folder.
Open the books and workbooks from the extracted folder. The instructor-video links open online.
Inside the extracted batch, open labs, then M00. Copy file-practice.zip into DE_Study\raw.
Extract that small archive into a new folder under practice. It contains source-note.txt,
orders.csv and a folder named evidence with a blank answer form. Open source-note.txt. It says
"Original delivery: 4 orders." Close it.
Select source-note.txt and press Ctrl+C. Open the extracted evidence folder and press Ctrl+V.
Rename the copied file attempt-01.txt. Open that copy and add a second line: "I checked the
delivery." Save it. Reopen the original source-note.txt and confirm it still has only its original
line. Now move attempt-01.txt from evidence into a new folder named completed using Ctrl+X,
open completed, then Ctrl+V. It should disappear from evidence and appear in completed.
What the result proves
The archive in raw remains available for a fresh extraction. The extracted source stays
unchanged. The edited attempt has a different name and location. Copying creates another
item; moving changes where the selected item lives. If a destination already contains a
same-named file, pause at the replace dialog and inspect both files. Keeping a new attempt
name is safer than guessing which version is disposable.
If something goes wrong
If you cannot save or linked files fail to open, check whether the address bar still shows the ZIP.
Extract and open the ordinary folder. If you cannot find a moved file, inspect the destination you
selected; a move does not leave a second copy behind. If you overwrote a practice file, preserve
what remains under a new name and extract a fresh copy from the untouched archive. That
recovery is possible because you kept the source archive.
Your independent practice
Copy the extracted orders.csv into completed as orders-attempt-01.csv. In Notepad change the
copied Pen quantity from 3 to 4, then save. Record which file has quantity 3 and which has
quantity 4. Keep both. Explain whether renaming the copy also renamed the original.
Changed retry - after your first review
Extract file-practice.zip into another new folder called recovery. Without changing any files, find
the original Pen quantity there and explain why it differs from your edited attempt.
Ready-made revision
Download first; extract the complete package; preserve raw; copy before editing; save attempts
with distinct names. Copy keeps the source. Move changes its location. Re-extracting an
untouched archive can recover a damaged practice input.

The job of this lesson
Prepare a small, understandable study environment. You need File Explorer, a browser, Notepad
and later VS Code and a spreadsheet application. You do not need Docker, Spark, a cloud
account or several databases for M00-M01. Complete DE00-03 first so you understand a
downloaded installer versus a data file.
Words before actions

rows: A program you use for a task

lines.text: Installer
A program that sets up another
application
a downloaded Windows setup file
Publisher
The organisation responsible for
software
Microsoft for VS Code
Version
An identifier for a software
release
record the version your screen shows
Administrator
An account with broader system
permissions
many personal tools do not need it
Installing more tools does not make a computer more ready for a lesson. Each extra tool adds
something else that can update, use memory or produce errors. Keep the browser, PDF reader
and one working application open while studying. Close unused applications if your 8 GB
computer slows down.
Follow with me once
Check whether VS Code is already installed using the Start menu search. If it opens, use Help,
About and record the version in setup-record.txt under evidence. An existing working
installation does not need reinstalling merely because a video shows an older interface.
If it is absent, open the official installation page linked below. Use its Windows download and
select User setup suitable for your machine. Read the publisher and filename in the browser
download. Run the completed installer and follow its displayed steps. User setup normally
installs for your account without administrator permissions. If this is a managed computer and
installation is blocked, record the restriction; do not bypass the organisation's controls. After
installation, launch VS Code from Start. Opening a blank editor is enough for this lesson. You will
create a file next.
For M01, check whether Excel already opens and whether you can edit and save a workbook. Do
not buy a subscription just to discover that an existing licence works. Record one of: desktop
Excel available; browser Excel available; spreadsheet access still unresolved. This batch's exact
click instructions use desktop Excel for Windows. Browser Excel can support much of the early
practice, but menus and Power Query availability differ. The written examples remain readable
while you resolve access. Mark software-dependent practice as pending until you actually
perform it; a video view is not a substitute for the lab.
Your setup record
Write your operating system as displayed in Settings, System, About; your editor and
spreadsheet application's names; whether each opens; where your course folder is; and any
unresolved error. You do not need to share a product key, account password or serial number. A
useful record says "Excel opens but I cannot save this file: [exact message]" rather than
"everything is broken."
If installation fails
First check whether the download completed and whether you selected Windows software.
Record the exact error and publisher. Try reopening the official instructions before trying
another installer. Do not disable antivirus, change PowerShell execution policy or run copied
administrator commands to make this introductory course work. If VS Code cannot be installed
today, use Notepad for the text exercises and leave the VS Code lesson's completion pending.
Your independent practice
Create setup-record.txt containing the four observations above. Close and reopen it. In
setup-record.txt, record the status of your editor and spreadsheet access. Explain the difference
between downloading a setup file and confirming that the installed application opens.
Changed retry - after your first review
Close VS Code, then reopen it from Start without opening the installer. Record its version again
and compare with your saved setup record. If unavailable, instead write the exact blocker and
the next official instruction you need.
Ready-made revision
Use official sources. Distinguish installer, installation and successful launch. Record actual
versions and blockers. Install tools when a lesson needs them. Current installation authority: VS
Code on Windows, checked 13 September 2026.

The job of this lesson
Open your own course folder, edit a text file, save it and find it outside the editor. Complete
DE00-04's VS Code setup first. This lesson does not require an extension, an AI assistant, a
programming language or a sign-in.
Words before actions
Word
Plain meaning
What to look for
Editor
An application for changing text
files
the central typing area
Explorer panel
VS Code's view of the opened
folder
filenames on the left
Tab
A label for an open editor
document
click to switch files
Unsaved change
An edit that is not yet written to
the file
often a dot on the tab
Workspace trust
A decision about enabling
features in a folder
trust only material you understand
Opening one file and opening its containing folder are different. A folder view helps you see the
input, working files and evidence together. The editor does not move those files into itself; it
displays files that still live on your drive.
Follow with me once
Launch VS Code. Use File, Open Folder. Choose the DE_Study folder you created, then Select
Folder. If a trust question appears, consider what this folder contains. For the files you
personally created in these exercises, you know the contents. For an unfamiliar downloaded
code project, keep it restricted until you understand it. Do not learn the habit of approving every
trust prompt automatically.
In the Explorer panel expand evidence and select folder-map.txt. You should see the text from
DE00-01. Add a new line: "Opened my study folder in VS Code." Press Ctrl+S. A dot on an
ordinary unsaved tab should clear after saving, although some interfaces use different
indicators. Close the file's tab, then open it again from the Explorer panel. Check that the new
line remains.
Use File, New Text File. Type two lines: "Lesson: DE00-05" and "Editor changes files on my
drive." Press Ctrl+Shift+S or use File, Save As. Save as editor-check.txt inside evidence. Check
that you selected evidence, because a new untitled file has no permanent location yet. Open
Windows File Explorer independently, visit evidence and open editor-check.txt in Notepad. Both
applications should show the same saved text.
Understand what happened
Before saving, your new text might exist only in the editor's working state. After saving, another
application can read it from the file. Reopening from File Explorer confirms the location and
contents. A separate study record describes your attempt and references its evidence. Saving
that record does not replace saving the actual file you edited.
You may see suggestions, extension recommendations or chat panels. None is required here.
Close a distracting side panel using its close button, or simply return to the file tab. Do not
install a Python extension for a lesson that only edits a text note.
If something goes wrong
If the left panel shows the wrong folder, use File, Open Folder and select DE_Study again. If your
changes disappear in Notepad, return to the editor and save, then reopen the file; compare both
paths if necessary. If a file is read-only, save a working copy inside your personal practice folder
and preserve the original. Do not change permissions on system directories.
Your independent practice
Create evidence\editor-attempt.txt with three lines: your lesson ID; your real course-folder path;
and one sentence distinguishing an editor from a folder. Save, close and reopen it in both VS
Code and Notepad. Record the evidence path in your saved attempt file.
Changed retry - after your first review
Make a copy named editor-retry.txt. Change only its final sentence to "This is my changed
retry." Open the original and copy to confirm that the original still has your first explanation.
Ready-made revision
Open the containing folder; inspect the actual filename; save; close; reopen. VS Code edits files
that remain on your drive. New text needs a filename and destination. You can study these
fundamentals without extensions or AI-generated code.
Evidence to keep: your attempt, the observed result and its explanation. Save the first attempt before

Instructor demonstration: Microsoft PowerShell for Beginners - Video 1 Learn PowerShell, 06:30-08:10. Meet
named commands. Our exact Get-Location, Get-ChildItem and Set-Location sequence is printed in the book; this
video segment is orientation. Stop manually at the listed end. Public title, creator, stable player runtime and
YouTube-displayed chapter boundaries inspected; full playback not verified.
The job of this lesson
Ask Windows where you are, list a folder and navigate to a child folder using three readable
commands. Complete the folder lessons first. Here we use Windows PowerShell, not Command
Prompt or a Linux shell. Different shells can use different commands; do not mix them without
checking.
Words before actions
Word
Plain meaning
Example
Terminal
A window for typing instructions
and reading responses
Windows Terminal
Shell
The program that interprets
those instructions
PowerShell
Command
One instruction to the shell
Get-Location
Current folder
The location relative paths start
from
your open practice folder
Argument
Extra information given to a
command
a path after -LiteralPath
A terminal is another way to work with the same filesystem. Clicking a folder in File Explorer
changes your browsing location; Set-Location changes the shell's location. Neither action moves
the actual files. The word Location in these commands means the place you are currently
looking from.
Follow with me once
Open PowerShell from the Start menu. A prompt often begins with PS and ends with >. Do not
type the displayed prompt; type only the command below and press Enter.
Get-Location
The response includes a Path heading and your current location. It might be your user folder.
Your result need not match a screenshot. Now open DE_Study in File Explorer, click the address
bar and copy its full path. In PowerShell type Set-Location -LiteralPath followed by that path in
single quotes. For example, only if this is your real path:
Set-Location -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\Ashish\Documents\DE_Study'
Get-Location
Get-ChildItem
Run one line at a time. Set-Location means change the shell's current location. -LiteralPath asks
it to use the path literally. The quoted text is one argument, which matters when folder names
contain spaces. Get-Location checks the result. Get-ChildItem lists the contents. You should
recognise raw, practice and evidence from File Explorer, even though PowerShell also shows
columns such as Mode and LastWriteTime.
Now run Set-Location -LiteralPath '.\practice', then Get-Location. A dot means the current folder;
.\practice therefore means the practice child of the folder you were in. Run Set-Location
-LiteralPath '..' to go back to the parent. Run Get-Location again. The two dots mean parent.
These commands navigate; they do not delete or rename anything.
What to compare
The final path should be DE_Study again. Listing it should show the same folder names as File
Explorer. An absolute path gives the whole location, often starting with a drive. A relative path
needs a starting point. If you are already inside evidence, .\practice means a child of evidence,
not the practice folder beside evidence. The same relative text can therefore succeed or fail
depending on your current folder.
If a command fails
Read the exact message and run Get-Location. "Cannot find path" often means a misspelling or
an unexpected current location. Copy your real path from File Explorer instead of guessing a
username. If Get-Location is "not recognized", check that you opened PowerShell. Do not install
software or change execution policy to repair a misspelled folder path. These commands do not
need a script file or administrator access.
Your independent practice
From DE_Study, navigate to evidence using a relative path, list its contents, then return to
DE_Study. Record the three commands, the final path and one existing filename you saw.
Explain why the relative path depends on your starting folder.
Changed retry - after your first review
From DE_Study, navigate directly to practice\first_attempt using one relative path, then use an
absolute path copied from File Explorer to return to evidence. Record the ending location.
Ready-made revision
Get-Location: where am I? Get-ChildItem: what is here? Set-Location: look from another folder.
Single quotes keep a path together. Dot means here; two dots mean parent. Check location
before changing anything else.
Evidence to keep: your attempt, the observed result and its explanation. Save the first attempt before
opening DE00-06 in the Explained Reviews book. After review, solve the changed retry and keep it as a
separate attempt.
Before starting: DE00-06. Video: Instructor watch ranges appear below. Read the vocabulary, perform

Instructor demonstration: Microsoft PowerShell for Beginners - Video 1 Learn PowerShell, 10:25-12:55. See
command help. Apply the book's one-change-at-a-time recovery to your own error; the video does not
demonstrate our deliberate missing-folder case. Stop manually at the listed end. Public title, creator, stable
player runtime and YouTube-displayed chapter boundaries inspected; full playback not verified.
The job of this lesson
Turn an error message into a small investigation you can explain. Complete DE00-06. An error is
evidence about a failed operation. It is not evidence that you are bad at computers. We will
deliberately request a folder that does not exist, without damaging any files.
Words before actions
Word
Plain meaning
In this lesson
Expected result
What should happen if the
operation works
entering the evidence folder
Actual result
What you observed
a path error
Reproduce
Repeat the same conditions and
see the result again
rerun the same command
Hypothesis
A possible cause you can test
a folder name was misspelled
Retest
Repeat the task after a specific
repair
use the correct path
Randomly changing five things creates a new problem: even if the task works, you do not know
which change mattered. A useful repair changes one relevant thing, then repeats the same
check. This is the beginning of debugging, the process of locating and correcting a cause of
failure.
Follow with me once
In PowerShell, use your actual absolute path to enter DE_Study. Run Get-Location and
Get-ChildItem. Confirm that evidence exists and that evidnce does not. Now deliberately run:
Set-Location -LiteralPath '.\evidnce'
You should get a message saying the path cannot be found. Read the folder spelling in the
message. Your current folder should remain DE_Study; check with Get-Location. The failed
navigation did not create the missing folder or erase your files.
Create error-01.txt under evidence. Record five things: the command; the starting location;
what you expected; the actual message; and your proposed cause. A strong proposed cause is
"the command says evidnce, but the folder listing says evidence." It compares two observations.
"PowerShell is broken" is much broader and is not supported by this evidence.
Repair only the spelling by running Set-Location -LiteralPath '.\evidence'. Check Get-Location
and Get-ChildItem. Add a final line to your error record: "Corrected the folder spelling; the final
path ends with evidence and its files are listed." Keep the failed command in the record. It
explains why the repair was necessary.
Know what your evidence does and does not show
The successful retest supports this repair for this failure. It does not prove that every future path
error has the same cause. Another error might involve a different current folder, unavailable
drive or access restriction. Begin with the message you actually have. If the command names a
file you did not intend to access, stop and inspect the path before trying again.
A useful help request includes the smallest relevant command and error, plus the expected
result and what you already tried. Hide passwords, access tokens and unrelated personal file
contents. Do not remove the spelling or path segment that is necessary to understand the
problem; you can replace a personal username consistently with YOUR_NAME.
Your independent practice
From DE_Study, try navigating to a missing folder named practce. Save the exact attempt and
error. Use the folder listing to identify the likely cause, repair it and record the successful ending
path. Explain why reinstalling PowerShell would not be the first useful step.
Changed retry - after your first review
Start inside evidence. Try Set-Location -LiteralPath '.\practice'. If evidence has no practice child,
it fails even though practice exists beside evidence. Diagnose this failure, then navigate to the
intended practice folder without creating a new one.
Ready-made revision
Record expected versus actual. Inspect the exact command and current location. Propose one
cause supported by observations. Change one thing and retest. Preserve the failed attempt and
explain the successful repair.
Evidence to keep: your attempt, the observed result and its explanation. Save the first attempt before

The job of this lesson
Use the book, practice files and explained reviews as one study workflow. You have now
created, saved, reopened and repaired real files. This lesson explains how to preserve that work
and decide what to practise next. You do not need an app to begin. A long study session or
completed video does not demonstrate a skill by itself.

An attempt can be wrong and still be valuable. It shows what you understood before seeing the
explanation. Replacing it with the correct answer removes that information. Keep attempt 1,
then add a repair or attempt 2. A retry must change a condition or question enough that you
have to think again.

What to keep, and what not to rewrite
The lesson already supplies revision notes. Read those notes when returning to the topic; do not
copy the whole explanation into your record. Your record needs only your own answer, observed
result, evidence path and any repair. The practical files are part of the work: a workbook shows
formulas that a sentence about finishing cannot show.
Suppose you write the path of editor-attempt.txt in a study record. That path tells you where to
find the file. It does not contain the external file's text automatically. If you move the course to
another computer, preserve both the study record and the actual evidence files. Update the
reference if the new location changes.
Make and check a backup
In File Explorer, copy the evidence folder into a separate backup location and give the copy a
dated name, such as evidence-backup-2026-09-13. Open that copied folder and reopen one
study record and its copied evidence file. Check that both contain what you expect. A
same-drive copy can help recover an accidental edit; it cannot protect against failure of that
drive. If available, keep another copy on a separate device or storage location you already use.
If an exercise fails, preserve the expected and actual results. For example, if Notepad shows an
old line, check whether you saved the edited file and whether both applications opened the
same path. After repair, reopen the file again. The successful retest should address the original
failure.
Your independent practice
Save a new study-record copy explaining how a file path differs from a file's contents. Include
the real path of editor-attempt.txt. Save and reopen both files. Copy both into a new backup
folder and reopen the copies. In your record, state what you checked and whether writing the
path alone would preserve the external text file.
Changed retry - after your first review
Save a separate retry record explaining one path error you repaired. Make a new dated backup
copy that includes the original attempt and this retry. Keep your earlier backup too. Reopen the
new backup and check that both records are present. Explain why the earlier backup cannot
contain work created after it was made.
Ready-made revision
Read, watch, do, attempt, review, repair, retry, explain, revisit. Keep original attempts. Use the
supplied revision notes. Record practical evidence, not pages of copied theory. Keep actual files
as well as their references. M00 is ready when you can locate, edit, save, reopen and repair a
file task independently.
